prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / product-mockup.
Edit target: the supplied Utkal tote/jhula design photograph. Change the bag's outer material from rough cotton canvas to NATURAL TASAR SILK: warm undyed golden-beige/copper-brown, fine irregular slub weave, subtle silk sheen visible under light, softly structured drape. It must look like premium woven silk, not burlap, jute, shiny satin, plastic, or coarse canvas.
Preserve the Utkal heritage graphics: strong deep sea-blue book-and-sailing-boat emblem and large uppercase English "UTKAL" wordmark, small laterite sun and restrained laterite border rules. No Odia in this English treatment, no extra text or brand. Keep the fabric visible around the print.
Refine construction tastefully for a daily-use lined Tasar Jhula: comfortable broad double shoulder handles with subtle visible reinforced stitching, a softly gusseted base, a small glimpse of plain natural cotton lining at the open top. Silk outer shell with internal support is a design proposal, not an authenticity certificate.
Keep the same warm ivory studio backdrop, tabletop, gentle natural shadows, full bag and handles in frame, front three-quarter product view. The finished visual should feel warm, tactile, contemporary and rooted in Odisha. No badges, certification marks, specification text, embroidery claims or watermark.
status: Concept only; fibre, origin and construction require a physical sample
